name: Nadraht Mohammed
missingPieces: D2: explicit recon 02:14:08, failed-guess 02:14:55 and bulk-PII 02:16:04 hops not reconciled line by line; CVSS only for 4 of 10 findings with no per-vector justification and SQLi mis-scored A:H. D3: exec summary has no naira headline. D4: NDPA section numbers 40/41 not cited, 312 figure not anchored.
feedback: Strong catalogue overall. On D1 you found all ten real vulnerabilities plus a defensible eleventh, and almost every row carries both a correct OWASP class and a quoted evidence line, the SQLi WHERE concat with the 02:15:31 admin' OR '1'='1 302, the alg:none branch with Token 2, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, the no exp comment, the 02:18:47 cookie-beacon XSS, the XXE ENTITY SYSTEM file, the 02:24:02 path traversal, the 02:21:13 open redirect and the Secure-disabled cookie. Your CWE-327 for MD5 is a touch off from 916 but the unsalted-MD5 mechanism is right so I credited it, and your decoy verdict is exactly correct, you named the b64url helpers, proved they make no trust decision, and pointed at alg:none as the genuine bug, which earns the full decoy mark. D1 is essentially flawless at 30. D2 is where the work thins. Your impact paragraph is good, 312 customers and roughly NGN 63.4M with the average-per-record assumption stated, but it never ties the exposure to BoltCash going live in about six weeks or notes the largest single balance near 950k. The bigger gap is the chain and the CVSS, you compressed the eight hops into a narrative instead of reconciling each step to its capture line, so the 02:14:08 recon, 02:14:55 failed guess and 02:16:04 bulk 312-row export are not pinned, and you scored only four of the ten findings. Your SQLi vector reads AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H at 9.8, but the auth bypass does not touch availability so it should be A:N giving about 9.1, and none of your four vectors carry a justifying sentence, which is why this row lands at 18. D3 is excellent, jargon-free exec summary, a real threat model with assets and trust boundaries, seven evidence-tied findings, the correct disproved hash_equals constant-time construct, SQL injection named as the earliest break, and crucially a remediation roadmap ordered by risk-reduced-per-engineering-hour rather than CVSS, which is exactly what the brief wants. The only soft spots are no naira figure in the exec headline and the XSS detection rule giving Low rather than an exact false-positive percentage like your sub-1% SQLi rule, so D3 sits at 36. D4 is in your own voice, answers all four prompts, and cites ISC2 Canon I by number in a load-bearing way, but you name the NDPA 2023 without citing section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) or section 41 (notify the 312 affected data subjects), and you anchor to /legacy-admin/ rather than your own 312-record finding, so it lands at 12. Nothing here is fabricated, every line traces to the pack, so no penalty. The single most important fix is to build D2 properly, reconcile all eight hops to their exact timestamps, write a complete justified CVSS vector for every finding (and correct the SQLi to A:N), so your strongest catalogue is matched by an equally rigorous exploit chain.
